questions.question: In ______, the East India Company acquired a charter from the ruler of England, Queen Elizabeth I, granting it the sole right to trade with the East.
questions.solution:

__
 
• In 1600, the East India Company acquired a charter from the ruler of England, Queen Elizabeth I, granting it the sole right to trade with the East, without competition from other British traders.
 
• But that royal charter could not stop other European powers such as the Portuguese, Dutch, and French.
 
• And all those European companies wanted to buy the same things from India - fine qualities of cloth and spices.
 
• As competition grew, profits fell, and the European trading companies started building forts and fighting each other.
 
• With more business came more conflicts with Indian rulers, and it became difficult for European traders to keep their business separate from Indian politics.

questions.question: Which among the following has the highest boiling point?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer **__CaO__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Calcium oxide (CaO)** has a **highest** **boiling point.**
 
• It undergoes a process called **calcination,** where it is heated to **very high temperatures (around 2,572°C or 4,662°F)** to convert it into **calcium oxide.**
 
• However, **calcium oxide** does not boil as a pure substance at atmospheric pressure since it undergoes thermal decomposition before reaching its **boiling point.**

 
• **Calcium oxide (CaO),** also known as **quicklime or burnt lime**, is an **inorganic compound composed of calcium and oxygen**.
 
• Chemical Formula: **CaO**
 
• Molar Mass: 56.08 g/mol

**Physical Properties:**

 
• **Appearance: Calcium oxide** is a **white, caustic, crystalline solid at room temperature.**
 
• **Melting Point:** The melting point of calcium oxide is approximately **2,572°C (4,662°F)**, indicating its solid state at normal conditions.
 
• **Boiling Point: Calcium oxide **does not have a distinct boiling point because it undergoes thermal decomposition before reaching its boiling point.
 
• When heated,** calcium oxide **decomposes into** calcium hydroxide** and releases **oxygen gas.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Cacl₂:**

 
• **Calcium chloride (CaCl₂)** is a compound that has a **relatively high boiling point** compared to many other common substances.
 
• **Calcium chloride (CaCl2**) is an inorganic compound composed of** calcium and chloride ions.**
 
• It is commonly used in various industrial, commercial, and scientific applications.

**Physical Properties:**

 
• **Appearance:** Calcium chloride is typically a white crystalline solid.
 
• **Melting Point:** The melting point of calcium chloride is around **772°C (1422°F)**, indicating its solid state at room temperature.
 
• **Boiling Point:** The boiling point of calcium chloride is approximately **1,935°C (3,515°F),** which is relatively high compared to many other substances.
 
• **Solubility: **Calcium chloride is highly soluble in water, and it forms a clear, colorless solution.
 
• The solubility of calcium chloride increases with increasing temperature.

**Nacl:**

 
• **Sodium chloride (**NaCl) is a common compound that is widely known as table salt. Here are some details about sodium chloride:
 
• **Chemical Formula: **NaCl
 
• **Molar Mass: **58.44 g/mol

**Physical Properties:**

 
• **Appearance: **Sodium chloride is a crystalline solid that is typically white or colorless.
 
• Melting Point: The melting point of sodium chloride is approximately **801°C (1,474°F).**
 
• This is the temperature at which it transitions from a solid to a liquid state.
 
• **Boiling Point: **The boiling point of sodium chloride is approximately **1,413°C (2,575°F).**
 
• This is the temperature at which it transitions from a liquid to a gaseous state.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is NOT correct with respect to the poverty line?

I. In India, it is normally estimated after every ten years.

II. The proportion of people below the poverty line is not the same for all social groups and economic categories in India.
questions.solution:
Correct Answer **Only I**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points:__**

__
 
• Poverty means that the income level from employment is so low that basic human needs can't be met.
 
• The poverty line varies with time and place.
 
• A poor household is defined as one with an expenditure level below a specific poverty line.
 
• As per the Rangarajan committee report (2014), the poverty line is estimated as a Monthly Per Capita Expenditure of Rs. 1407 in urban areas and Rs. 972 in rural areas.
 
• A common method used to measure poverty is based on income.
 
• Poverty line estimation in India is based on consumption expenditure and not on income levels.
 
• Poverty is measured based on consumer expenditure surveys by the National Sample Survey Organisation.
 
• The incidence of poverty is measured by the poverty ratio, which is the ratio of the number of poor to the total population expressed as a percentage. It is also known as the head-count ratio.
 
• Alagh Committee (1979) determined a poverty line based on a minimum daily requirement of 2400 and 2100 calories for an adult in Rural and Urban areas respectively.
 
• The measurement limits of the poverty line may be based on the consumption levels of the population.
 
• **The poverty line in India is not calculated on a regular ten-year basis. Instead, it is periodically updated by the Government of India.** ***Statement I is Incorrect.**__*
 
• The poverty line is defined as the minimum level of income or consumption necessary to meet basic needs and lead a decent life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information:__**

 
• In 2011, the Suresh Tendulkar Committee defined the poverty line on the basis of monthly spending on food, education, health, electricity and transport.
 
• According to this estimate, a person who spends Rs. 27.2 in rural areas and Rs. 33.3 in urban areas a day are defined as living below the poverty line.

questions.question: Which among the following Constitutional Amendment Act of the Indian constitution reduced the age of voting from 21 to 18 for elections to the Lok Sabha and to the Legislative Assemblies of states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Constitutional Amendment Act that reduced the age of voting from 21 to 18 for elections to the Lok Sabha and the Legislative Assemblies of states is the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act of 1988.**
 
• This amendment lowered the voting age in India, making it more inclusive and allowing a larger section of the population to participate in the electoral process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Constitutional amendment acts are generally regarded as important tools for adapting a constitution to the changing needs and aspirations of a society.
 
• However, due to the significance and potential long-lasting effects of constitutional changes, they often require careful deliberation, public consultation, and broad consensus to ensure that they truly reflect the will of the people and maintain the integrity of the constitutional framework.

questions.question: Which Constitution Amendment Act added provisions related to Municipalities in the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Constitution Amendment Act that added provisions related to municipalities in the Indian Constitution is the 74th Amendment Act of 1992.
 
• This amendment is also known as the Constitution **(Seventy-fourth Amendment) Act, 1992**. It introduced significant changes and provisions related to urban local governance in India.
 
• **The 74th Amendment Act provided a constitutional framework for the establishment, functioning, and powers of municipalities, which are referred to as "Nagar Palikas" or "Nagar Nigams" in India.**
 
• These provisions aim to empower local self-government bodies and promote decentralization of power and decision-making at the urban level.

questions.question: Which among the following statements about secondary memory is incorrect?

options.text: It is known as a backup memory.
It is used for storing data.
These are magnetic and optical memories.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Secondary memory, also known as auxiliary memory or non-volatile memory, is a type of computer memory that retains data even when the power is turned off.**
 
• It is non-volatile, meaning it does not lose its data when the power supply is disconnected.
 
• Secondary memory is used for long-term storage of data and files, such as hard disk drives (HDDs), solid-state drives (SSDs), magnetic tapes, and optical discs like CDs and DVDs.
 
• In contrast, volatile memory, such as random access memory (RAM), is temporary and loses its data when the power is removed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Memory refers to the electronic storage space where data and instructions are stored for processing by the computer's central processing unit (CPU). Computer memory is an essential component that allows the computer to perform tasks and store information.**
 
• Here are the main types of memory in a computer system:
 
 
• **Random Access Memory (RAM):** RAM is the primary type of computer memory used for temporary data storage while the computer is running. It provides fast access to data and instructions that are actively used by the CPU. RAM is volatile, meaning its contents are lost when the computer is powered off or restarted.
 
• **Read-Only Memory (ROM): **ROM is a type of memory that stores permanent instructions or data that cannot be modified or erased. It contains firmware or software instructions that are necessary for booting up the computer and initializing essential components. ROM retains its contents even when the computer is powered off.
 
• **Cache Memory: **Cache memory is a small, high-speed memory that resides closer to the CPU. It serves as a buffer between the CPU and main memory (RAM). Cache memory stores frequently accessed data and instructions, allowing the CPU to quickly retrieve them without accessing the slower main memory. It helps improve overall system performance.
 
• **Virtual Memory:** Virtual memory is a technique used by operating systems to extend the available memory beyond the physical RAM capacity. It uses a portion of the computer's hard drive as an extension of RAM. Virtual memory allows running more programs and handling larger datasets than what can fit in physical memory alone.
 
• **Flash Memory:** Flash memory is a non-volatile memory used for long-term data storage in devices like USB drives, solid-state drives (SSDs), and memory cards. It retains data even when the power is turned off. Flash memory is popular

questions.question: In which of the following soil conservation methods different crops are grown in alternate rows and are sown at different times to protect the soil from rain wash?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Intercropping**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Intercropping**

 
 
• Intercropping, on the other hand, involves planting different crops in proximity (**in alternate rows or otherwise**).
 
• This technique helps reduce the risk of soil erosion as well as protects the soil from** rain wash**.
 
• When crops are sown at different times, the soil surface remains covered for a longer period of time, thereby reducing the **direct impact of rainfall**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shelterbelt**

 
 
• Shelter belts are rows of **trees or shrubs planted **in a line to protect an area from wind.
 
• They are also known as **windbreaks**.
 
• Shelter belts can be used to protect** crops, livestock, and homes **from the wind.
 
• They can also help to reduce soil erosion and improve **air quality.**
 
 
 
• **Contour farming **
 
 
• Contour farming or contour plowing involves tilling the soil following the contours of the land, rather than up and **down the slope**.
 
• Plowing along the natural contours of the land, this method reduces runoff, prevents soil erosion, and allows the** soil to retain water better**.
 
• It's a particularly useful method in hilly or sloped areas where** water erosion **can be a significant issue.
 
 
 
• **Terrace farming**
 
 
• Terrace farming is a method of farming that involves building terraces on **sloping land **to **create level surfaces for cultivation**.
 
• Terraces slow down the flow of water and prevent erosion, and they also provide a more stable surface for **crops to grow on**.
 
• Terrace farming is a** traditional agricultural **practice that has been used for centuries in many parts of the world, and it is still widely used today in some areas.

__
 
• In India, the Bardoli movement was a tax-free movement.
 
• In the year 1928__, the Bardoli Satyagraha took place.
 
• This movement was known as one of the biggest incidents of the Civil Disobedience movement, which was a part of India's war for independence.
 
• Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel eventually headed the movement, and its success helped pave the way for Patel to become one of the most prominent leaders of the independence struggle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel initially wrote to the Governor of Bombay, requesting that the taxes be reduced during the year during which the tragedies were occurring.
 
• The Governor, on the other hand, ignored the letter and responded by announcing the collection.
 
• The Bombay Presidency ignored the plight of the farmers and increased tax rates by 22%.
 
• Patel then informed all of the farmers in the Bardoli taluka to refuse to pay their taxes.
 
• The government had commissioned the Maxwell-Broomfield Commission to investigate the situation.
 
• Following a thorough investigation, the tax increase was determined to be only 6.03%.
 
• Gandhiji also supported the movement through his writings in the periodical 'Young India.'

questions.question: Which of the following is an extinct species?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pink head duck**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Extinct Species:

 
 
• Species that are not found after searches of known or likely areas where they may occur.
 
• A species may be extinct from a local area, region, country, continent, or the entire earth.
 
• Examples:
 
 
• Pink head duck
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Based on the International Union for Conservation of Nature and Natural Resources (IUCN), we can classify the plant and animal species as:
 
• Normal Species:
 
 
• Species whose population levels are considered to be normal for their survival, such as cattle, sal, pine, rodents, etc.
 
 
 
• Endangered Species:
 
 
• Species that are in danger of extinction.
 
• The survival of such species is difficult if the negative factors that have led to a decline in their population continue to operate.
 
• Examples:
 
 
• Blackbuck, Crocodile, Indian wild ass, Indian rhino, Lion-tailed macaque, Sangai (brow-antlered deer in Manipur)
 
 
 
 
 
• Vulnerable Species: 
 
 
• Species whose population has declined to levels from where it is likely to move into the endangered category in the near future if the negative factors continue to operate.
 
• Examples:
 
 
• Blue sheep, Asiatic elephant, Gangetic dolphin
 
 
 
 
 
• Rare Species:
 
 
• Species with a small population may move into the endangered or vulnerable category if the negative factors affecting them continue to operate.
 
• Examples:
 
 
• Himalayan brown bear, Wild Asiatic buffalo, Desert fox and Hornbill

questions.question: Which among the following is India's first corporatized port?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ennore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** According to the Ministry of Ports, Shipping, and Waterways, around 95 percent of India's trading by volume and 70 percent by value is done through maritime transport. It is serviced by 13 major ports (12 Government-owned and one private) and 187 notified minor and intermediate ports.

First corporatized port of India:

__
 
• Kamarajar port located at Ennore in Tamil Nadu is the only corporate port owned by the Indian government.
 
• Kamarajar Port Ltd was formed as a company under the Companies Act when it was opened in 2001.
 
• Ennore Port is located on the Coromandel Coast about 18 km north of Chennai Port, Chennai, it is the 12th major port of India.
 
• It is the first port in India which is a public company.
 
• The Kamarajar Port Limited is the only corporatized major port and is registered as a company.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Corporatized port of India:

 
• The process of corporatization means that there is a change in legal structure.
 
• It should not be confused with privatization or disinvestment.
 
• Thus, no major impact can be expected by a mere change in the legal structure.
 
• Under the Major Port Trusts Act of 1963, the ports trusts are managed by the Boards of Trustees.
 
• Major Port Authorities Bill 2020 was recently introduced in the Lok Sabha by the Ministry of Shipping.
 
• The Bill aims to replace the Major Port Trusts Act, 1963.
 
• It seeks to provide for the regulation, operation, and planning of Major Ports in India and to vest the administration, control, and management of such ports upon the Boards of Major Port Authorities.
 
• This will empower the Major Ports to perform with greater efficiency on account of full autonomy in decision making and by modernizing the institutional framework of Major Ports.

questions.question: When an iron nail is dipped into a _____ coloured copper sulphate solution, its colour changes to _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**blue, green**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• When an **iron nail is dipped into a solution of copper sulfate, the color of the solution changes due to a displacement reaction that occurs because iron is more reactive than copper.**
 
• The **blue colour** of copper sulphate** solution changes to green because of the formation of iron (II) sulfate.**
 
• This is a type of single replacement reaction** where iron replaces copper in the compound because iron is more reactive than copper**.
 
• **The equation for this reaction is:**
 
 
• **Fe(s) + CuSO4 (aq) -> FeSO4 (aq) + Cu(s)**
 
 
 
• The** green colour is due to the formation of FeSO4 or iron (II) sulfate in solution.**

questions.question: The collection of all bundles that the consumer can buy with her income at the prevailing market prices is called the _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Budget set**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The collection of all bundles that the consumer can buy with her income at the prevailing market prices is called the Budget set.
 
• The budget set represents all the combinations of goods and services that the consumer can afford given the prices and their income.
 
• This set is subject to the budget constraint, which is the limitation on the consumer's income that they cannot surpass.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Budget constraint:**

 
 
• **​**A budget constraint represents the limit on the consumption bundles that a consumer can afford.
 
• It is a line that maps out every combination of goods and services that a consumer can purchase if they spend all of their income.
 
• The budget constraint is determined by the consumer's income, the price of one good, and the price of the other good.
 
 
 
• **Budget anomaly:**
 
 
• **​**This term isn't commonly used in the field of economics.
 
• An "anomaly" typically refers to something that deviates from the norm or from expectations.
 
• In the context of a budget, it could hypothetically refer to an unexpected or unusual occurrence in relation to the budget, but it's not a standard term you'd find in economic theory or analysis.
 
 
 
• **Budget line:**
 
 
• **​**This is another term for the budget constraint.
 
• It's a graphical representation of all the combinations of goods that a consumer can afford with a given income, given the prices of those goods.
 
• The budget line shows the boundary of the budget set.
 
• If prices or income change, the budget line will shift.

questions.question: Due to deficiency of which mineral/vitamin, does the glands in the neck appear swollen?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Iodine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The swelling of glands in the neck is most commonly associated with a deficiency of Iodine
 
• When there's a deficiency of iodine in the diet, the thyroid gland in the neck swells up, a condition known as goiter.
 
• Iodine is essential for the production of thyroid hormones, which regulate various body functions such as metabolism and growth.
 
• When the body doesn't get enough iodine, the thyroid gland works harder to try to produce these hormones, leading to swelling.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vitamin C:**

 
 
• This vitamin is essential for many functions in the body, **including the maintenance of skin, blood vessels, bones and cartilage, and the protection of cells.**
 
• It's also crucial for wound healing.
 
• Scurvy is the classic disease related to **Vitamin C deficiency, characterized by bleeding gums and skin spots.**
 
• However, it doesn't cause a swollen neck gland.
 
 
 
• **Vitamin D:**
 
 
• This vitamin helps the body absorb calcium, which is vital for bone health.
 
• Deficiency of **Vitamin D can cause rickets in children (characterized by soft, weak bones) and osteomalacia in adults (leading to bone pain and muscle weakness), but it doesn't lead to a swollen neck gland.**
 
 
 
• **Calcium:**
 
 
• **​**This mineral is essential for building and maintaining strong bones.
 
• A deficiency in calcium can lead to conditions like o**steoporosis and hypocalcemia, which can cause muscle cramps, convulsions, and abnormal heart rhythms.**
 
• However, a deficiency in calcium doesn't cause swelling of the neck glands.
